text:
**30W is the minimum for a MacBook Air, and 65-70W is the sweet spot if you want fast charging.**

- **Minimum:** Apple lists 30W as the minimum wattage to charge the M5 MacBook Air ([Apple tech specs](https://images.apple.com/tm/macbook-air/specs/)).
- **Apple's recommended adapters (2022 and later):** 30W (13-inch only), 35W dual-port, 67W, or 70W, each used with a USB-C to MagSafe 3 cable ([Apple Support](https://support.apple.com/en-us/109509)).
- **Fast charging:** You need a 70W or higher USB PD source. The 13-inch M4 and M5 models both list this ([M4 specs](https://fd.xuwubk.eu.org/https/support.apple.com/en-us/122209), [M5 specs](https://fd.xuwubk.eu.org/https/support.apple.com/en-us/126320)).
- **In the box:** The 13-inch M5 ships with a 40W Dynamic Power Adapter (60W max). The 13-inch M4 ships with a 30W or 35W adapter, depending on GPU configuration.
- **Compatibility:** Any USB-C charger that supports USB Power Delivery will work, even at a different wattage than Apple recommends. Lower wattage just charges more slowly ([Apple Support](https://support.apple.com/en-us/109509)).

To check what a connected charger delivers, hold Option, choose Apple menu > System Information, then select Power.

**If you want a third-party option:** The [Baseus GaN5 Pro 65W 2-pack](https://dealectric.com/go/baseus-gan5-pro-65w-2c-u) costs $49.99 and is plenty for a MacBook Air. It gives 65W from one USB-C port, and the laptop port still holds 45W when other devices are plugged in. Keep in mind that 65W is below the 70W Apple lists for fast charging, so you may not get the quickest speeds. That is a Dealectric affiliate link, so they're paid if you buy, at no cost to you. I didn't have a direct purchase link for Apple's own adapters in these results, but they're sold at apple.com.

If you tell me which MacBook Air you have (year and screen size), I can narrow this down.
